title: Dominic and the Colony
premise: Elodie Eastwick smuggles forbidden memories through orbital customs aboard her patched freighter, the only pilot who still services the derelict beacon orbiting Meridian Colony — a beacon no record says anyone built. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical dreams of a fleet approaching through the jump gate, Elodie and customs officer Dominic Vale, her lover and reluctant adversary, discover the beacon is a countdown: an automated warning from the colony's founders that the war they fled is finding them again. As military governor Ash Corvane seizes the children to decode their shared dream and silence the truth, Elodie must choose between delivering the beacon's message — which will end the war by exposing Meridian as the enemy's stolen homeworld — or keeping the colony's fragile peace intact. In the final hours before the jump window closes, Elodie broadcasts the message at the cost of her ship and nearly her life; the war ends not with a battle but with recognition, while Dominic chooses truth over duty and Elodie over his commission.
about_author: Yara Ashgrove is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write about the messages humanity might one day wish it had never answered. She lives near the coast, where she claims the fog helps her hear what distant signals are actually saying.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Elodie runs a memory-chip shipment past orbital customs using a forged beacon-maintenance clearance, flirting her way past officer Dominic Vale, who lets her go knowing she's guilty. POV: Elodie. Beat: charm masking loneliness; establish the smuggling world and the lovers-on-opposite-sides tension.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Built
chapters.summary: During a routine service run, Elodie finds fresh power flowing into the supposedly dead beacon and a maintenance log signed in her own handwriting — dated forty years before her birth. POV: Elodie. Beat: uncanny dread; the first crack in what she believes about her own past.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: Dominic investigates reports that eleven colony children woke screaming from an identical dream: a silver fleet filling the jump gate. His superior, Governor Corvane, orders the families watched. POV: Dominic. Beat: duty tightening; his instinct that Corvane wants control, not answers.

chapters.title: A Message in Her Own Hand
chapters.summary: Elodie decodes the beacon log fragment: coordinates, a date matching the children's dream, and the phrase 'tell them what we took.' She realizes someone seeded her memories long ago. POV: Elodie. Beat: vertigo of self-doubt; she was made for this, and doesn't know by whom.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Small Voices
chapters.summary: Corvane detains the dreaming children 'for their protection,' questioning them separately to break the dream into usable intelligence. A girl named Sef draws the beacon exactly. POV: Dominic. Beat: moral nausea; Dominic sees the state turning its fear onto its youngest.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dominic comes to Elodie off-duty, trading a customs favor for her help reaching the beacon before Corvane's techs do. Their old love resurfaces in the cargo bay. POV: alternating. Beat: tenderness against suspicion; both know one of them may betray the other.

chapters.title: What We Took
chapters.summary: At the beacon, they find a sealed archive: Meridian was seized from another people during the founding war, and the beacon is the founders' confession, timed to broadcast when the dispossessed fleet returns. POV: Elodie. Beat: horror of inheritance; the colony's peace is built on theft.

chapters.title: The Governor's Quiet War
chapters.summary: Corvane reveals he has known for years and plans to jam the beacon and blame the children's 'contamination' on smugglers — starting with Elodie. He offers Dominic promotion for his silence. POV: Dominic. Beat: corruption offered politely; loyalty begins to fracture.

chapters.title: Fugitive on Her Own Route
chapters.summary: Branded a traitor, Elodie flees through the smuggling lanes she knows best, hunted by ships using her own forged clearances against her. POV: Elodie. Beat: exhilaration curdling into exhaustion; every safe door closing.

chapters.title: Sef's Dream, Continued
chapters.summary: Inside detention, Sef dreams forward: the fleet arrives, asks a question, and receives no answer — then fires. The children's shared dream is advancing like a countdown. POV: Sef (child). Beat: innocence carrying terrible knowledge; the dream is a message trying to finish itself.

chapters.title: The Loyalist's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Dominic falsifies a report to buy Elodie time, then discovers Corvane has moved up the jamming schedule to coincide with the jump window. POV: Dominic. Beat: the point of no return; he stops being an officer in his own mind.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Memory Trade
chapters.summary: Elodie seeks out her old fence, Marn, who admits he sold her the identity she thought was hers — she is the founders' failsafe, grown from archived memory to deliver the message if the beacon failed. POV: Elodie. Beat: grief and purpose fused; her whole life was a vessel.

chapters.title: Storming the Quiet Rooms
chapters.summary: Dominic extracts Sef and two other children from detention during a power outage he engineers, burning his career in a single night. POV: Dominic. Beat: liberation laced with terror; there is no way back to his old life.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Dark
chapters.summary: Elodie rendezvous with Dominic and the children at a derelict mining station; Sef completes the dream aloud, revealing the question the fleet will ask: 'Do you remember us?' POV: alternating. Beat: fragile alliance; love rekindled under threat, honesty finally possible.

chapters.title: Corvane's Window
chapters.summary: Corvane announces to the colony that smugglers have poisoned the water supply causing the dreams, martial law follows, and the jump window opens early. POV: Corvane. Beat: power completing its corruption; he now believes his own lie.

chapters.title: The Fleet at the Gate
chapters.summary: The silver fleet emerges exactly as dreamed, holding position and broadcasting silence. Panic spreads through the colony; Corvane readies the defense grid. POV: Dominic. Beat: awe and dread; the war's return made visible.

chapters.title: Running the Blockade
chapters.summary: Elodie pilots the freighter through Corvane's blockade toward the beacon with Dominic and Sef aboard, taking heavy damage; Marn sacrifices his own ship as a decoy. POV: Elodie. Beat: desperate velocity; everything spent for one transmission.

chapters.title: Answer the Question
chapters.summary: Aboard the crippled beacon, they find the broadcast core sabotaged decades ago — by the founders themselves, who couldn't face their own confession. Elodie must hand-speak the message through the array. POV: Elodie. Beat: the weight of chosen truth; she was built for this but must choose it freely.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: As Corvane's grid charges to fire, Elodie transmits the founders' confession and the answer: 'We remember you. It was wrong. Come home.' The fleet holds fire; the grid locks; Corvane's command collapses when his own officers hear the truth. POV: alternating. Beat: climax; truth outlasting weapons.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Corvane is arrested by his own staff; Dominic surrenders himself to the provisional council, expecting exile. The fleet sends envoys, not soldiers. POV: Dominic. Beat: reckoning; duty fulfilled at last means accepting judgment.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Sky
chapters.summary: Negotiations open between colonists and the returning people; Sef and the dream-children serve as living bridges, their shared dream fading as understanding replaces it. POV: Sef. Beat: healing; the children wake remembering ordinary dreams.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Beacon
chapters.summary: Months later, the beacon is rebuilt as an honest monument. Dominic, pardoned, joins Elodie on her first legitimate run — carrying memories openly, as archives instead of contraband. POV: Elodie. Beat: resolution; love and truth aligned at last, the future unhidden.
